qs.q: The study will report an odds ratio of 2.0 with a 95 % confidence interval of 1.2–3.3. How should this result be interpreted?
o: The interval shows precise evidence of an association
The interval reflects strong statistical significance
The interval suggests no statistical significance
The interval denotes a positive association
qs.e: An odds ratio >1 whose confidence interval does not include 1 (1.2–3.3) shows a statistically significant positive association. The other options mischaracterize the interval.

qs.q: A cohort study examines the relationship between extended working hours and major depressive disorder among healthcare workers, reporting an odds ratio of 1.75. Which reported statistical parameter best reflects the precision of this estimated effect size?
qs.e: The 95% confidence interval indicates the range of values within which the true population effect size likely falls, with a narrower interval reflecting higher precision. The p-value indicates statistical significance relative to the null hypothesis but does not quantify the precision of the point estimate.

qs.q: A patient with systemic lupus erythematosus develops new-onset psychosis and depression. Which autoantibody has a strongly established odds ratio for these specific psychiatric manifestations?
qs.e: Anti-ribosomal-P antibodies carry a 4 to 10 times odds ratio for psychosis and depression in SLE patients. Other antibodies like anti-SCL-70 are typically associated with scleroderma rather than lupus-related psychiatric symptoms.
